questions.text: Your company built a TensorFlow neutral-network model with a large number of neurons and layers. The model fits well for the training data. However, when tested against new data, it performs poorly. What method can you employ to address this?
questions.html: Your company built a TensorFlow neutral-network model with a large number of neurons and layers. The model fits well for the training data. However, when tested against new data, it performs poorly. What method can you employ to address this?

choices.text: Threading
choices.html: Threading

choices.text: Serialization
choices.html: Serialization

choices.text: Dropout Methods
choices.html: Dropout Methods

choices.text: Dimensionality Reduction
choices.html: Dimensionality Reduction

questions.sourceExplanation: The symptoms described—strong performance on training data but poor performance on new data—are the definition of overfitting. Dropout is a regularization technique that prevents overfitting by randomly disabling neurons during training, forcing the network to learn more robust features and improving generalization. Threading addresses computational speed, serialization handles model persistence, and dimensionality reduction modifies input features, none of which directly solve the structural overfitting issue caused by excessive model complexity.

questions.sourceExplanation:
Option B is correct because truncated exponential backoff is the standard best practice for handling transient database failures in Google App Engine applications. This strategy prevents overwhelming an unresponsive database with excessive connection attempts while ensuring eventual recovery without indefinite blocking.

In contrast, Option C creates a thundering herd problem that can prevent recovery, Option D provides data too stale for a weather app, and Option A is an operational task outside the scope of frontend logic.

questions.text: You are building new real-time data warehouse for your company and will use Google BigQuery streaming inserts. There is no guarantee that data will only be sent in once but you do have a unique ID for each row of data and an event timestamp. You want to ensure that duplicates are not included while interactively querying data. Which query type should you use?
questions.html: You are building new real-time data warehouse for your company and will use Google BigQuery streaming inserts. There is no guarantee that data will only be sent in once but you do have a unique ID for each row of data and an event timestamp. You want to ensure that duplicates are not included while interactively querying data. Which query type should you use?

choices.text: Include ORDER BY DESK on timestamp column and LIMIT to 1.
choices.html: Include ORDER BY DESK on timestamp column and LIMIT to 1.

choices.text: Use GROUP BY on the unique ID column and timestamp column and SUM on the values.
choices.html: Use GROUP BY on the unique ID column and timestamp column and SUM on the values.

choices.text: Use the LAG window function with PARTITION by unique ID along with WHERE LAG IS NOT NULL.
choices.html: Use the LAG window function with PARTITION by unique ID along with WHERE LAG IS NOT NULL.

choices.text: Use the ROW_NUMBER window function with PARTITION by unique ID along with WHERE row equals 1.
choices.html: Use the ROW_NUMBER window function with PARTITION by unique ID along with WHERE row equals 1.

questions.sourceExplanation:
To handle duplicates from BigQuery streaming inserts, you must deduplicate rows based on the unique ID. 
The ROW_NUMBER() window function assigned over PARTITION BY unique ID allows you to rank duplicate rows and filter for only the first occurrence (WHERE row = 1). 
This ensures exactly one row per unique ID is returned, whereas GROUP BY aggregates data rather than removing duplicates, LAG filters out unique records, and ORDER BY with LIMIT returns a single row globally.

questions.text: Your company is in a highly regulated industry. One of your requirements is to ensure individual users have access only to the minimum amount of information required to do their jobs. You want to enforce this requirement with Google BigQuery. Which three approaches can you take? (Choose three.)

You want to enforce this requirement with Google BigQuery. Which three approaches can you take? (Choose three.)

choices.text: Disable writes to certain tables.
choices.html: Disable writes to certain tables.

choices.text: Restrict access to tables by role.
choices.html: Restrict access to tables by role.

choices.text: Ensure that the data is encrypted at all times.
choices.html: Ensure that the data is encrypted at all times.

choices.text: Restrict BigQuery API access to approved users.
choices.html: Restrict BigQuery API access to approved users.

choices.text: Segregate data across multiple tables or databases.
choices.html: Segregate data across multiple tables or databases.

choices.text: Use Google Stackdriver Audit Logging to determine policy violations.
choices.html: Use Google Stackdriver Audit Logging to determine policy violations.

questions.sourceExplanation:
To enforce the principle of least privilege in BigQuery, you must actively restrict access and structure data for granular control. 
Restricting access to tables by role (B) ensures users only have permissions necessary for their specific job functions. 
Segregating data across multiple tables or datasets (E) allows for finer-grained access controls, preventing users from seeing unrelated sensitive information. 
Restricting BigQuery API access to approved users (D) limits the pool of individuals who can query data at all. 
Options A, C, and F are incorrect because read-only status still implies access beyond minimum needs, encryption is a default transparency measure not an access control, and audit logging detects rather than prevents unauthorized access.

Which Google database service should you use?

Which Google database service should you use?

choices.html: BigQuery

choices.text: Cloud Bigtable
choices.html: Cloud Bigtable

questions.sourceExplanation:
The requirement to avoid managing infrastructure scaling points to a fully managed, serverless database that scales automatically.
Cloud SQL requires manual configuration for CPU and memory scaling (vertical scaling), whereas Cloud Datastore (Firestore in Datastore mode) handles scaling transparently.
Additionally, Google explicitly lists financial transactions as a use case for Cloud Datastore due to its ACID transaction support, making it the superior choice for this specific workload.
questions.explanation: The listed services omit some modern alternatives. Decide from transactional boundaries, consistency, scale and access pattern; the historical Datastore name alone is not a payment-system design.

questions.html: You need to store and analyze social media postings in Google BigQuery at a rate of 10,000 messages per minute in near real-time. Initially, design the application to use streaming inserts for individual postings. Your application also performs data aggregations right after the streaming inserts. You discover that the queries after streaming inserts do not exhibit strong consistency, and reports from the queries might miss in-flight data. How can you adjust your application design?

choices.text: Re-write the application to load accumulated data every 2 minutes.
choices.html: Re-write the application to load accumulated data every 2 minutes.

choices.html: Convert the streaming insert code to batch load for individual messages.

choices.html: Estimate the average latency for data availability after streaming inserts, and always run queries after waiting twice as long.

questions.sourceExplanation:
BigQuery streaming inserts provide eventual consistency, meaning data may not be immediately available for querying due to internal buffering.
Option D is the correct answer in the context of this exam question because it suggests adjusting the application logic to wait for a period longer than the estimated latency (e.g., twice the average) before running queries, ensuring the data has been flushed and is visible.
This approach acknowledges the inherent delay of streaming inserts without switching to batch loads or external databases, which would violate the near real-time requirement.
questions.explanation: Waiting twice an observed average does not bound worst-case freshness or prove strong consistency. Design around documented write visibility, delivery contracts and explicit completeness checks rather than treating an average delay as a guarantee. The original key is preserved for comparison only.

choices.html: Your custom endpoint is not acknowledging messages within the acknowledgement deadline.

questions.sourceExplanation:
Google Cloud Pub/Sub guarantees at-least-once delivery and redelivers messages if the push endpoint fails to send a valid HTTP 200 response within the acknowledgement deadline.
If the custom endpoint does not acknowledge messages in time, Pub/Sub treats them as unprocessed and retries delivery, resulting in duplicates.

Company Overview -
Flowlogistic is a leading logistics and supply chain provider. They help businesses throughout the world manage their resources and transport them to their final destination. The company has grown rapidly, expanding their offerings to include rail, truck, aircraft, and oceanic shipping.

- Tomcat `" Java services

choices.text: Store he common data in the HDFS storage for a Google Cloud Dataproc cluster.

questions.sourceExplanation:
Google Cloud Storage (GCS) serves as the central data lake in Google Cloud Platform, providing a unified storage layer for both BigQuery and Dataproc (Hadoop/Spark).
Avro is an open-source serialization format that is natively supported by both systems, allowing them to read the same common data without duplication or complex connector configurations.
Storing data in BigQuery tables (A/B) creates silos for Hadoop workloads, while HDFS on Dataproc (D) is ephemeral and not suitable for long-term shared storage across different processing engines.

However, they are unable to deploy it because their technology stack, based on Apache Kafka, cannot support the processing volume. Flowlogistic architecture resides in a single data center:
✑ Databases
8 physical servers in 2 clusters
- SQL Server `" user data, inventory, static data
3 physical servers
- Cassandra `" metadata, tracking messages
10 Kafka servers `" tracking message aggregation and batch insert
✑ Application servers `" customer front end, middleware for order/customs
60 virtual machines across 20 physical servers
- Tomcat `" Java services
- Nginx `" static content
- Batch servers
✑ Storage appliances
- iSCSI for virtual machine (VM) hosts
- Fibre Channel storage area network (FC SAN) `" SQL server storage
- Network-attached storage (NAS) image storage, logs, backups
✑ 10 Apache Hadoop /Spark servers
- Core Data Lake
- Data analysis workloads
✑ 20 miscellaneous servers
- Jenkins, monitoring, bastion hosts,

Business Requirements -
✑ Build a reliable and reproducible environment with scaled panty of production.
✑ Aggregate data in a centralized Data Lake for analysis
✑ Use historical data to perform predictive analytics on future shipments
✑ Accurately track every shipment worldwide using proprietary technology
✑ Improve business agility and speed of innovation through rapid provisioning of new resources
✑ Analyze and optimize architecture for performance in the cloud

questions.text:
MJTelco Case Study -

Company Overview -
MJTelco is a startup that plans to build networks in rapidly growing, underserved markets around the world. The company has patents for innovative optical communications hardware. Based on these patents, they can create many reliable, high-speed backbone links with inexpensive hardware.

Company Background -
Founded by experienced telecom executives, MJTelco uses technologies originally developed to overcome communications challenges in space. Fundamental to their operation, they need to create a distributed data infrastructure that drives real-time analysis and incorporates machine learning to continuously optimize their topologies. Because their hardware is inexpensive, they plan to overdeploy the network allowing them to account for the impact of dynamic regional politics on location availability and cost.
Their management and operations teams are situated all around the globe creating many-to-many relationship between data consumers and provides in their system. After careful consideration, they decided public cloud is the perfect environment to support their needs.

Solution Concept -
MJTelco is running a successful proof-of-concept (PoC) project in its labs. They have two primary needs:
✑ Scale and harden their PoC to support significantly more data flows generated when they ramp to more than 50,000 installations.
✑ Refine their machine-learning cycles to verify and improve the dynamic models they use to control topology definition.
MJTelco will also use three separate operating environments `" development/test, staging, and production `" to meet the needs of running experiments, deploying new features, and serving production customers.

Business Requirements -
✑ Scale up their production environment with minimal cost, instantiating resources when and where needed in an unpredictable, distributed telecom user community.
✑ Ensure security of their proprietary data to protect their leading-edge machine learning and analysis.
✑ Provide reliable and timely access to data for analysis from distributed research workers
✑ Maintain isolated environments that support rapid iteration of their machine-learning models without affecting their customers.

Technical Requirements -
✑ Ensure secure and efficient transport and storage of telemetry data
✑ Rapidly scale instances to support between 10,000 and 100,000 data providers with multiple flows each.
✑ Allow analysis and presentation against data tables tracking up to 2 years of data storing approximately 100m records/day
✑ Support rapid iteration of monitoring infrastructure focused on awareness of data pipeline problems both in telemetry flows and in production learning cycles.

CEO Statement -
Our business model relies on our patents, analytics and dynamic machine learning. Our inexpensive hardware is organized to be highly reliable, which gives us cost advantages. We need to quickly stabilize our large distributed data pipelines to meet our reliability and capacity commitments.

CTO Statement -
Our public cloud services must operate as advertised. We need resources that scale and keep our data secure. We also need environments in which our data scientists can carefully study and quickly adapt our models. Because we rely on automation to process our data, we also need our development and test environments to work as we iterate.

CFO Statement -
The project is too large for us to maintain the hardware and software required for the data and analysis. Also, we cannot afford to staff an operations team to monitor so many data feeds, so we will rely on automation and infrastructure. Google Cloud's machine learning will allow our quantitative researchers to work on our high-value problems instead of problems with our data pipelines.
MJTelco's Google Cloud Dataflow pipeline is now ready to start receiving data from the 50,000 installations. You want to allow Cloud Dataflow to scale its compute power up as required. Which Cloud Dataflow pipeline configuration setting should you update?

questions.sourceExplanation:

questions.sourceExplanation:
Bigtable rowkeys must be designed to avoid hotspotting by ensuring writes are distributed across multiple nodes. Using 'date' or 'timestamp' as the leading component of a rowkey creates severe write hotspots because all devices update on the same time interval, overwhelming specific nodes.

Option A is the best available choice because placing 'date' first groups data chronologically, which supports the most common query pattern (retrieving all data for a given device on a given day) efficiently via range scans. While an ideal schema might reverse this or use salting to balance writes, Option A effectively satisfies the read-heavy analytical requirement without creating the extreme concentration of writes that pure timestamp keys cause.

questions.sourceExplanation:
To prevent combinatorial index explosion caused by multi-valued properties (actors and tags) combined with an ordered property (date_released), you must manually configure composite indexes in the `index.yaml` file.
Datastore automatically creates all combinations of indexes unless explicitly defined; manual configuration limits creation to only the specific query patterns needed (e.g., actors + date_released, tags + date_released), drastically reducing index entry counts.

questions.sourceExplanation:
Option C is correct because using `gsutil` with parallel uploads (`-m`) efficiently handles a high volume of small files by leveraging multi-threading, overcoming the per-file overhead inherent in the current SFTP design.
Option D is correct because aggregating many small 4 KB files into larger TAR archives reduces the overhead associated with numerous individual TCP connections and storage object creation operations, which significantly improves throughput for Cloud Storage.
Options A, B, and E are incorrect: bandwidth is already sufficient (utilization is low), compression adds unnecessary CPU overhead for tiny text files, and Storage Transfer Service requires higher bandwidth thresholds (>300 Mbps) than the available 50 Mbps.

questions.sourceExplanation:
The query plan image indicates a significant imbalance in the processing stages, which is a hallmark of data skew.
When most rows share the same key value (e.g., 'country'), BigQuery cannot evenly distribute the work across workers during the shuffle phase, causing some nodes to process disproportionately more data than others.
This uneven distribution forces the query to wait for the slowest worker to finish, resulting in the observed delay regardless of concurrency or partition count.

choices.html: Y2

questions.sourceExplanation: The data exhibits a circular decision boundary, which is non-linear in the original X-Y space. A linear classifier requires features that are linearly separable; by adding the synthetic feature X² + Y², the data becomes separable because points inside the circle have smaller values than those outside. This transformation maps the radial distance from the origin, allowing a linear model to distinguish the classes effectively.

questions.text:
MJTelco Case Study -

Company Overview -
MJTelco is a startup that plans to build networks in rapidly growing, underserved markets around the world. The company has patents for innovative optical communications hardware. Based on these patents, they can create many reliable, high-speed backbone links with inexpensive hardware.

Company Background -
Founded by experienced telecom executives, MJTelco uses technologies originally developed to overcome communications challenges in space. Fundamental to their operation, they need to create a distributed data infrastructure that drives real-time analysis and incorporates machine learning to continuously optimize their topologies. Because their hardware is inexpensive, they plan to overdeploy the network allowing them to account for the impact of dynamic regional politics on location availability and cost.
Their management and operations teams are situated all around the globe creating many-to-many relationship between data consumers and provides in their system. After careful consideration, they decided public cloud is the perfect environment to support their needs.

Solution Concept -
MJTelco is running a successful proof-of-concept (PoC) project in its labs. They have two primary needs:
✑ Scale and harden their PoC to support significantly more data flows generated when they ramp to more than 50,000 installations.
✑ Refine their machine-learning cycles to verify and improve the dynamic models they use to control topology definition.
MJTelco will also use three separate operating environments `" development/test, staging, and production `" to meet the needs of running experiments, deploying new features, and serving production customers.

Business Requirements -
✑ Scale up their production environment with minimal cost, instantiating resources when and where needed in an unpredictable, distributed telecom user community.
✑ Ensure security of their proprietary data to protect their leading-edge machine learning and analysis.
✑ Provide reliable and timely access to data for analysis from distributed research workers
✑ Maintain isolated environments that support rapid iteration of their machine-learning models without affecting their customers.

Technical Requirements -
Ensure secure and efficient transport and storage of telemetry data
Rapidly scale instances to support between 10,000 and 100,000 data providers with multiple flows each.
Allow analysis and presentation against data tables tracking up to 2 years of data storing approximately 100m records/day
Support rapid iteration of monitoring infrastructure focused on awareness of data pipeline problems both in telemetry flows and in production learning cycles.

CEO Statement -
Our business model relies on our patents, analytics and dynamic machine learning. Our inexpensive hardware is organized to be highly reliable, which gives us cost advantages. We need to quickly stabilize our large distributed data pipelines to meet our reliability and capacity commitments.

CTO Statement -
Our public cloud services must operate as advertised. We need resources that scale and keep our data secure. We also need environments in which our data scientists can carefully study and quickly adapt our models. Because we rely on automation to process our data, we also need our development and test environments to work as we iterate.

CFO Statement -
The project is too large for us to maintain the hardware and software required for the data and analysis. Also, we cannot afford to staff an operations team to monitor so many data feeds, so we will rely on automation and infrastructure. Google Cloud's machine learning will allow our quantitative researchers to work on our high-value problems instead of problems with our data pipelines.
MJTelco is building a custom interface to share data. They have these requirements:
1. They need to do aggregations over their petabyte-scale datasets.
2. They need to scan specific time range rows with a very fast response time (milliseconds).
Which combination of Google Cloud Platform products should you recommend?

Flowlogistic Case Study -

Company Overview -
Flowlogistic is a leading logistics and supply chain provider. They help businesses throughout the world manage their resources and transport them to their final destination. The company has grown rapidly, expanding their offerings to include rail, truck, aircraft, and oceanic shipping.

Company Background -
The company started as a regional trucking company, and then expanded into other logistics market. Because they have not updated their infrastructure, managing and tracking orders and shipments has become a bottleneck. To improve operations, Flowlogistic developed proprietary technology for tracking shipments in real time at the parcel level. However, they are unable to deploy it because their technology stack, based on Apache Kafka, cannot support the processing volume. In addition, Flowlogistic wants to further analyze their orders and shipments to determine how best to deploy their resources.

Solution Concept -
Flowlogistic wants to implement two concepts using the cloud:
✑ Use their proprietary technology in a real-time inventory-tracking system that indicates the location of their loads
✑ Perform analytics on all their orders and shipment logs, which contain both structured and unstructured data, to determine how best to deploy resources, which markets to expand info. They also want to use predictive analytics to learn earlier when a shipment will be delayed.

Existing Technical Environment -
Flowlogistic architecture resides in a single data center:
✑ Databases
- 8 physical servers in 2 clusters
- SQL Server `" user data, inventory, static data
- 3 physical servers
- Cassandra `" metadata, tracking messages
10 Kafka servers `" tracking message aggregation and batch insert
✑ Application servers `" customer front end, middleware for order/customs
- 60 virtual machines across 20 physical servers
- Tomcat `" Java services
- Nginx `" static content
- Batch servers
✑ Storage appliances
- iSCSI for virtual machine (VM) hosts
- Fibre Channel storage area network (FC SAN) `" SQL server storage
Network-attached storage (NAS) image storage, logs, backups
✑ 10 Apache Hadoop /Spark servers
- Core Data Lake
- Data analysis workloads
✑ 20 miscellaneous servers
- Jenkins, monitoring, bastion hosts,

Business Requirements -
✑ Build a reliable and reproducible environment with scaled panty of production.
✑ Aggregate data in a centralized Data Lake for analysis
✑ Use historical data to perform predictive analytics on future shipments
✑ Accurately track every shipment worldwide using proprietary technology
✑ Improve business agility and speed of innovation through rapid provisioning of new resources
✑ Analyze and optimize architecture for performance in the cloud
✑ Migrate fully to the cloud if all other requirements are met

Technical Requirements -
✑ Handle both streaming and batch data
✑ Migrate existing Hadoop workloads
✑ Ensure architecture is scalable and elastic to meet the changing demands of the company.
✑ Use managed services whenever possible
✑ Encrypt data flight and at rest
Connect a VPN between the production data center and cloud environment

SEO Statement -
We have grown so quickly that our inability to upgrade our infrastructure is really hampering further growth and efficiency. We are efficient at moving shipments around the world, but we are inefficient at moving data around.
We need to organize our information so we can more easily understand where our customers are and what they are shipping.

CTO Statement -
IT has never been a priority for us, so as our data has grown, we have not invested enough in our technology. I have a good staff to manage IT, but they are so busy managing our infrastructure that I cannot get them to do the things that really matter, such as organizing our data, building the analytics, and figuring out how to implement the CFO' s tracking technology.

CFO Statement -
Part of our competitive advantage is that we penalize ourselves for late shipments and deliveries. Knowing where out shipments are at all times has a direct correlation to our bottom line and profitability. Additionally, I don't want to commit capital to building out a server environment.
Flowlogistic's management has determined that the current Apache Kafka servers cannot handle the data volume for their real-time inventory tracking system.
You need to build a new system on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) that will feed the proprietary tracking software. The system must be able to ingest data from a variety of global sources, process and query in real-time, and store the data reliably. Which combination of GCP products should you choose?

After migrating ETL jobs to run on BigQuery, you need to verify that the output of the migrated jobs is the same as the output of the original. You've loaded a table containing the output of the original job and want to compare the contents with output from the migrated job to show that they are identical. The tables do not contain a primary key column that would enable you to join them together for comparison.
What should you do?

choices.text: Select random samples from the tables using the RAND() function and compare the samples.
choices.html: Select random samples from the tables using the RAND() function and compare the samples.

choices.text: Select random samples from the tables using the HASH() function and compare the samples.
choices.html: Select random samples from the tables using the HASH() function and compare the samples.

choices.text: Use a Dataproc cluster and the BigQuery Hadoop connector to read the data from each table and calculate a hash from non-timestamp columns of the table after sorting. Compare the hashes of each table.
choices.html: Use a Dataproc cluster and the BigQuery Hadoop connector to read the data from each table and calculate a hash from non-timestamp columns of the table after sorting. Compare the hashes of each table.

choices.text: Create stratified random samples using the OVER() function and compare equivalent samples from each table.
choices.html: Create stratified random samples using the OVER() function and compare equivalent samples from each table.

questions.sourceExplanation:
The requirement is to verify that the outputs are identical, which necessitates comparing every record rather than relying on random samples that might miss discrepancies. Since a primary key join is not possible, calculating a deterministic hash of the sorted non-timestamp columns for the entire dataset provides a reliable method to confirm total data parity.
Option C correctly implements this full-data verification strategy using Dataproc and the BigQuery connector.

Your Spark job is a complicated analytical workload that consists of many shuffling operations and initial data are parquet files (on average 200-400 MB size each). You see some degradation in performance after the migration to Dataproc, so you'd like to optimize for it. You need to keep in mind that your organization is very cost-sensitive, so you'd like to continue using Dataproc on preemptibles (with 2 non-preemptible workers only) for this workload.
What should you do?

choices.html: Increase the size of your parquet files to ensure them to be 1 GB minimum.

choices.html: Switch to TFRecords formats (appr. 200MB per file) instead of parquet files.

choices.text: Switch from HDDs to SSDs, copy initial data from GCS to HDFS, run the Spark job and copy results back to GCS.
choices.html: Switch from HDDs to SSDs, copy initial data from GCS to HDFS, run the Spark job and copy results back to GCS.

choices.text: Switch from HDDs to SSDs, override the preemptible VMs configuration to increase the boot disk size.
choices.html: Switch from HDDs to SSDs, override the preemptible VMs configuration to increase the boot disk size.

questions.sourceExplanation:
Option D is correct because the workload involves heavy shuffling, which is I/O intensive and benefits significantly from SSDs over HDDs for local disk operations. Additionally, preemptible VMs default to smaller boot disks that can become a bottleneck during shuffle phases, so overriding this configuration to increase disk size optimizes performance without violating the cost-sensitive constraint of using preemptibles.

Options C is incorrect because it incurs significant data transfer costs and latency by moving data in and out of HDFS. Options A and B are less effective; while file sizing matters, the existing 200-400MB range is generally acceptable for Parquet, and switching formats or slightly increasing size does not address the primary I/O bottleneck of shuffle operations on preemptible nodes.

questions.sourceExplanation:
The requirement to migrate a relational database without significant application refactoring necessitates a managed relational service compatible with standard SQL engines like MySQL, PostgreSQL, or SQL Server.
Cloud SQL supports these engines directly, allowing for a lift-and-shift migration that minimizes code changes and typically offers lower operational costs compared to globally distributed systems.
Cloud Spanner is a fully managed relational database but requires significant refactoring due to its proprietary nature and lack of features like stored procedures, while Bigtable and Firestore are NoSQL databases unsuitable for direct relational migration.

questions.sourceExplanation:
BigQuery charges based on the amount of data scanned per query. Without partitioning, filters on date columns still trigger full table scans across all three years of data, leading to high costs.
By partitioning the table by a TIMESTAMP or DATE column (Option A), BigQuery can perform partition pruning, scanning only the specific partitions relevant to the 30–90 day query window. This significantly reduces scan volume and cost while maintaining standard SQL query capabilities.

Cloud Bigtable distributes data based on row keys, and using a sequential or monotonic timestamp as the beginning of the key causes write hotspots because all new data targets the same tablet.
By prefixing the row key with the stock symbol (a high-cardinality attribute), writes are distributed across multiple tablets in parallel, eliminating the bottleneck.
This design follows best practices for time-series data in Bigtable to ensure balanced load distribution.

questions.sourceExplanation: Cloud Composer (Airflow) is the recommended solution for orchestrating complex data workflows on Google Cloud, specifically handling dependencies between sequential and concurrent tasks via Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs). While Dataproc Workflow Templates define job order, they do not natively support scheduling or the broader orchestration flexibility required by the question. Cloud Composer integrates seamlessly with Dataproc to schedule these templates or jobs, providing the necessary automation for both timing and dependency management.

choices.text: The current epoch time
choices.html: The current epoch time

choices.text: A concatenation of the product name and the current epoch time
choices.html: A concatenation of the product name and the current epoch time

choices.text: A random universally unique identifier number (version 4 UUID)
choices.html: A random universally unique identifier number (version 4 UUID)

choices.text: The original order identification number from the sales system, which is a monotonically increasing integer
choices.html: The original order identification number from the sales system, which is a monotonically increasing integer

questions.sourceExplanation:
Cloud Spanner partitions data based on the primary key to distribute load across nodes. Monotonically increasing keys (like epoch time or sequential integers) cause write hotspots because all new inserts target the same node's tail end.
Using a Version 4 UUID generates random values, ensuring an even distribution of writes across all nodes and maximizing throughput for transactional data.

questions.sourceExplanation: According to Cloud Dataflow documentation, major changes to windowing algorithms or triggering strategies are not compatible with in-place updates and may cause unpredictable results. Therefore, you cannot use the --update option for these significant structural changes. To ensure no data is lost during such a transition, you must stop the existing pipeline using the Drain option, which allows pending windows to close and process buffered data before termination.

questions.sourceExplanation:
The 'Trust No One' (TNO) model ensures that the cloud provider cannot access your data, which requires using Customer-Supplied Encryption Keys (CSEK) where Google Cloud never stores the keys.
Among the CSEK options, storing the key in a different project accessible only to the security team isolates it from general operational access and prevents accidental exposure or unauthorized decryption by non-security personnel.
questions.explanation: Customer-supplied server-side encryption keys do not imply that the provider can never decrypt data during processing. If the requirement is truly that the provider never receives plaintext or keys, evaluate a client-side encryption design and its query limitations. The imported “Trust No One” claim is stronger than the stated mechanism.

Your subscriber is not set up to retain acknowledged messages. What should you do to ensure that you can recover from errors after deployment?

choices.html: Set up the Pub/Sub emulator on your local machine. Validate the behavior of your new subscriber logic before deploying it to production.

choices.text: Create a Pub/Sub snapshot before deploying new subscriber code. Use a Seek operation to re-deliver messages that became available after the snapshot was created.

choices.text: Use Cloud Build for your deployment. If an error occurs after deployment, use a Seek operation to locate a timestamp logged by Cloud Build at the start of the deployment.
choices.html: Use Cloud Build for your deployment. If an error occurs after deployment, use a Seek operation to locate a timestamp logged by Cloud Build at the start of the deployment.

choices.text: Enable dead-lettering on the Pub/Sub topic to capture messages that aren't successfully acknowledged. If an error occurs after deployment, re-deliver any messages captured by the dead-letter queue.
choices.html: Enable dead-lettering on the Pub/Sub topic to capture messages that aren't successfully acknowledged. If an error occurs after deployment, re-deliver any messages captured by the dead-letter queue.

questions.sourceExplanation:
Creating a snapshot before deployment captures the subscription's state at that point in time. If new code erroneously acknowledges messages (causing them to be removed from the queue), the Seek operation against the snapshot resets the consumer to the pre-deployment state, allowing the re-delivery of all messages published since the snapshot was taken.

Other options fail because Dead-lettering (D) only captures messages that fail to process or are not acknowledged, whereas snapshots specifically address message loss due to premature acknowledgement. While Timestamp Seeking (C) is a recovery method, it requires retaining acknowledged messages on the subscription/topic, which the question states is not configured.

questions.sourceExplanation:
The question specifically highlights the use of SideInputs as a potential performance bottleneck. While SideInputs are efficient for small datasets, they require the entire PCollection to be loaded into memory on each worker, which can severely degrade performance and cause timeouts if the data is large or changes frequently.

CoGroupByKey is the recommended alternative for joining datasets when the side input data does not fit efficiently in memory, as it processes the join within the pipeline's shuffle stage rather than relying on global caching. This change allows Dataflow to scale the join operation horizontally across workers, thereby expediting job completion.

questions.text:
You are building a real-time prediction engine that streams files, which may contain PII (personal identifiable information) data, into Cloud Storage and eventually into BigQuery. You want to ensure that the sensitive data is masked but still maintains referential integrity, because names and emails are often used as join keys.
How should you use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API (DLP API) to ensure that the PII data is not accessible by unauthorized individuals?
questions.html:
You are building a real-time prediction engine that streams files, which may contain PII (personal identifiable information) data, into Cloud Storage and eventually into BigQuery. You want to ensure that the sensitive data is masked but still maintains referential integrity, because names and emails are often used as join keys.
How should you use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API (DLP API) to ensure that the PII data is not accessible by unauthorized individuals?

choices.text: Create a pseudonym by replacing the PII data with cryptogenic tokens, and store the non-tokenized data in a locked-down button.
choices.html: Create a pseudonym by replacing the PII data with cryptogenic tokens, and store the non-tokenized data in a locked-down button.

choices.text: Redact all PII data, and store a version of the unredacted data in a locked-down bucket.
choices.html: Redact all PII data, and store a version of the unredacted data in a locked-down bucket.

choices.text: Scan every table in BigQuery, and mask the data it finds that has PII.
choices.html: Scan every table in BigQuery, and mask the data it finds that has PII.

choices.text: Create a pseudonym by replacing PII data with a cryptographic format-preserving token.
choices.html: Create a pseudonym by replacing PII data with a cryptographic format-preserving token.

questions.sourceExplanation: The requirement to maintain referential integrity (allowing joins on names/emails) necessitates a deterministic transformation where identical inputs produce identical outputs. Format-Preserving Encryption (FPE) or Deterministic Encryption ensures this consistency while masking the data, whereas simple redaction destroys join keys and standard hashing may alter data format or be considered irreversible without lookup tables not specified in the option.
questions.reviewNote: Imported answer and rationale have not been independently verified. The official links below are related reading, not an official answer key.

questions.text: You are migrating an application that tracks library books and information about each book, such as author or year published, from an on-premises data warehouse to BigQuery. In your current relational database, the author information is kept in a separate table and joined to the book information on a common key. Based on Google's recommended practice for schema design, how would you structure the data to ensure optimal speed of queries about the author of each book that has been borrowed?
questions.html: You are migrating an application that tracks library books and information about each book, such as author or year published, from an on-premises data warehouse to BigQuery. In your current relational database, the author information is kept in a separate table and joined to the book information on a common key. Based on Google's recommended practice for schema design, how would you structure the data to ensure optimal speed of queries about the author of each book that has been borrowed?

choices.text: Keep the schema the same, maintain the different tables for the book and each of the attributes, and query as you are doing today.
choices.html: Keep the schema the same, maintain the different tables for the book and each of the attributes, and query as you are doing today.

choices.text: Create a table that is wide and includes a column for each attribute, including the author's first name, last name, date of birth, etc.
choices.html: Create a table that is wide and includes a column for each attribute, including the author's first name, last name, date of birth, etc.

choices.text: Create a table that includes information about the books and authors, but nest the author fields inside the author column.
choices.html: Create a table that includes information about the books and authors, but nest the author fields inside the author column.

choices.text: Keep the schema the same, create a view that joins all of the tables, and always query the view.
choices.html: Keep the schema the same, create a view that joins all of the tables, and always query the view.

questions.sourceExplanation:
Google recommends denormalizing data in BigQuery to improve query performance by avoiding expensive JOIN operations.
Nesting related fields (like author details) within the main table allows you to store hierarchical relationships efficiently without flattening every attribute into individual columns.

questions.text: You need to give new website users a globally unique identifier (GUID) using a service that takes in data points and returns a GUID. This data is sourced from both internal and external systems via HTTP calls that you will make via microservices within your pipeline. There will be tens of thousands of messages per second and that can be multi-threaded. and you worry about the backpressure on the system. How should you design your pipeline to minimize that backpressure?
questions.html: You need to give new website users a globally unique identifier (GUID) using a service that takes in data points and returns a GUID. This data is sourced from both internal and external systems via HTTP calls that you will make via microservices within your pipeline. There will be tens of thousands of messages per second and that can be multi-threaded. and you worry about the backpressure on the system. How should you design your pipeline to minimize that backpressure?

choices.text: Call out to the service via HTTP.
choices.html: Call out to the service via HTTP.

choices.text: Create the pipeline statically in the class definition.

choices.text: Create a new object in the startBundle method of DoFn.
choices.html: Create a new object in the startBundle method of DoFn.

choices.text: Batch the job into ten-second increments.
choices.html: Batch the job into ten-second increments.

questions.sourceExplanation: Processing tens of thousands of messages per second with individual synchronous HTTP calls creates significant backpressure due to high latency and concurrency limits. Batching requests into time increments reduces the total number of external API calls, smoothing out load spikes and preventing the external service from becoming a bottleneck.

The files being transferred are not large in number, but each file is 90 GB.
Additionally, you want your transactional systems to continually update the warehouse on Google Cloud in real time. What tools should you use to migrate the data and ensure that it continues to write to your warehouse?
questions.html:
You are migrating your data warehouse to Google Cloud and decommissioning your on-premises data center. Because this is a priority for your company, you know that bandwidth will be made available for the initial data load to the cloud. The files being transferred are not large in number, but each file is 90 GB.
Additionally, you want your transactional systems to continually update the warehouse on Google Cloud in real time. What tools should you use to migrate the data and ensure that it continues to write to your warehouse?

choices.text: Storage Transfer Service for the migration; Pub/Sub and Cloud Data Fusion for the real-time updates
choices.html: Storage Transfer Service for the migration; Pub/Sub and Cloud Data Fusion for the real-time updates

choices.text: BigQuery Data Transfer Service for the migration; Pub/Sub and Dataproc for the real-time updates

questions.sourceExplanation: gsutil is the recommended tool for initial data migration when sufficient network bandwidth is available and the total data volume is manageable (less than ~10TB), making it suitable for the few large files described. For real-time updates, Pub/Sub ingests change data capture events from on-premises systems, while Dataflow processes these streams continuously to write incremental updates to BigQuery.

questions.text: You are using Bigtable to persist and serve stock market data for each of the major indices. To serve the trading application, you need to access only the most recent stock prices that are streaming in. How should you design your row key and tables to ensure that you can access the data with the simplest query?
questions.html: You are using Bigtable to persist and serve stock market data for each of the major indices. To serve the trading application, you need to access only the most recent stock prices that are streaming in. How should you design your row key and tables to ensure that you can access the data with the simplest query?

choices.text: Create one unique table for all of the indices, and then use the index and timestamp as the row key design.
choices.html: Create one unique table for all of the indices, and then use the index and timestamp as the row key design.

choices.text: Create one unique table for all of the indices, and then use a reverse timestamp as the row key design.
choices.html: Create one unique table for all of the indices, and then use a reverse timestamp as the row key design.

choices.text: For each index, have a separate table and use a timestamp as the row key design.
choices.html: For each index, have a separate table and use a timestamp as the row key design.

choices.text: For each index, have a separate table and use a reverse timestamp as the row key design.
choices.html: For each index, have a separate table and use a reverse timestamp as the row key design.

questions.explanation: A shared table with an index identifier followed by time lets a query restrict a row-key range for that index. To simplify newest-first access, consider a reversed timestamp after that high-cardinality prefix or a supported reverse-read pattern. Avoid a timestamp-only leading key that concentrates writes. A is the closest listed layout, with this query-order qualification.

questions.text: You are building a report-only data warehouse where the data is streamed into BigQuery via the streaming API. Following Google's best practices, you have both a staging and a production table for the data. How should you design your data loading to ensure that there is only one master dataset without affecting performance on either the ingestion or reporting pieces?
questions.html: You are building a report-only data warehouse where the data is streamed into BigQuery via the streaming API. Following Google's best practices, you have both a staging and a production table for the data. How should you design your data loading to ensure that there is only one master dataset without affecting performance on either the ingestion or reporting pieces?

choices.text: Have a staging table that is an append-only model, and then update the production table every three hours with the changes written to staging.
choices.html: Have a staging table that is an append-only model, and then update the production table every three hours with the changes written to staging.

choices.text: Have a staging table that is an append-only model, and then update the production table every ninety minutes with the changes written to staging.
choices.html: Have a staging table that is an append-only model, and then update the production table every ninety minutes with the changes written to staging.

choices.text: Have a staging table that moves the staged data over to the production table and deletes the contents of the staging table every three hours.
choices.html: Have a staging table that moves the staged data over to the production table and deletes the contents of the staging table every three hours.

choices.text: Have a staging table that moves the staged data over to the production table and deletes the contents of the staging table every thirty minutes.
choices.html: Have a staging table that moves the staged data over to the production table and deletes the contents of the staging table every thirty minutes.

questions.sourceExplanation: The correct design involves moving data from staging to production and clearing the staging table, as maintaining an append-only staging table leads to unbounded growth and performance issues. Google best practices recommend a three-hour interval for this process because the BigQuery streaming buffer retains data for up to 90 minutes (rarely longer), making 3 hours sufficient to ensure all streamed rows are available for DML operations like DELETE or MERGE without failing due to buffering locks.

Exporting Cloud Logging data to BigQuery via a sink (Answer A) is the recommended best practice for scalable, queryable log analysis.
BigQuery allows for efficient aggregation and complex filtering using SQL views on structured logs, whereas CSV exports to Cloud Storage (Answers B and D) require external processing and lack native analytical capabilities.
Answer C suggests importing after filtering, but exporting directly to BigQuery retains all raw log data for comprehensive reporting flexibility.

Development Team to be able to read data from both Cloud Storage and BigQuery, but the External Team should only be able to read data from BigQuery. What should you do?
questions.html:
The Development and External teams have the project viewer Identity and Access Management (IAM) role in a folder named Visualization. You want the
Development Team to be able to read data from both Cloud Storage and BigQuery, but the External Team should only be able to read data from BigQuery. What should you do?

choices.text: Remove Cloud Storage IAM permissions to the External Team on the acme-raw-data project.
choices.html: Remove Cloud Storage IAM permissions to the External Team on the acme-raw-data project.

choices.html: Create Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) firewall rules on the acme-raw-data project that deny all ingress traffic from the External Team CIDR range.

choices.text: Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter containing both projects and BigQuery as a restricted API. Add the External Team users to the perimeter's Access Level.
choices.html: Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter containing both projects and BigQuery as a restricted API. Add the External Team users to the perimeter's Access Level.

choices.text: Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter containing both projects and Cloud Storage as a restricted API. Add the Development Team users to the perimeter's Access Level.
choices.html: Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter containing both projects and Cloud Storage as a restricted API. Add the Development Team users to the perimeter's Access Level.

questions.sourceExplanation:
VPC Service Controls define security perimeters that restrict access to specific services. To allow the Development Team access to both Cloud Storage and BigQuery while denying the External Team access to Cloud Storage, you must create a perimeter containing Cloud Storage as a restricted service.
By adding only the Development Team users to the perimeter's Access Level, they are granted access inside the boundary, whereas the External Team remains outside and is denied access to the restricted Cloud Storage resources.

questions.explanation: Interconnect plus Storage Transfer Service is the listed managed private-network approach. However, “a few hours” depends on provisioned end-to-end capacity. One decimal petabyte over 100 Gbit/s needs about 22.2 hours at ideal utilization; more capacity is needed for a shorter target. The option is a design direction, not a timing guarantee.

questions.text: You are developing a new deep learning model that predicts a customer's likelihood to buy on your ecommerce site. After running an evaluation of the model against both the original training data and new test data, you find that your model is overfitting the data. You want to improve the accuracy of the model when predicting new data. What should you do?
questions.html: You are developing a new deep learning model that predicts a customer's likelihood to buy on your ecommerce site. After running an evaluation of the model against both the original training data and new test data, you find that your model is overfitting the data. You want to improve the accuracy of the model when predicting new data. What should you do?

choices.text: Increase the size of the training dataset, and increase the number of input features.
choices.html: Increase the size of the training dataset, and increase the number of input features.

choices.text: Increase the size of the training dataset, and decrease the number of input features.
choices.html: Increase the size of the training dataset, and decrease the number of input features.

choices.text: Reduce the size of the training dataset, and increase the number of input features.
choices.html: Reduce the size of the training dataset, and increase the number of input features.

choices.text: Reduce the size of the training dataset, and decrease the number of input features.
choices.html: Reduce the size of the training dataset, and decrease the number of input features.

questions.sourceExplanation: Overfitting occurs when a model learns noise or irrelevant patterns in the training data, often due to excessive complexity relative to the amount of data. Decreasing the number of input features reduces this complexity (feature selection), helping prevent the model from fitting to noise. Simultaneously, increasing the size of the training dataset provides more examples for the model to learn general patterns rather than memorizing specific instances, thereby improving accuracy on new, unseen data.

Data freshness measures the delay between event time and processing completion, while system lag measures only the duration of active processing. 
Since data freshness is high (40s) but system lag is low (5s), individual messages process quickly, indicating a large backlog exists in the subscription rather than slow per-message execution. 
The job cannot ingest new messages as fast as they arrive, causing accumulated delay; thus, increasing throughput via optimization or scaling workers resolves the backlog.

questions.sourceExplanation: Rotating a key (Option A) does not automatically re-encrypt existing data, and changing the default CMEK on an existing bucket (Option B) only affects future writes, leaving old data encrypted with the compromised key. To re-encrypt all data, you must copy objects to a new location where they are protected by the new key. Option D is superior because creating a new bucket with the new key as the default ensures both the copied data and any future uploads are automatically protected by the new CMEK, whereas Option C requires explicit key specification for every copy operation but does not guarantee protection for subsequent manual uploads if the bucket's default encryption isn't explicitly set or managed consistently.

choices.text: Use AEAD functions and delete keys when employees leave the organization.
choices.html: Use AEAD functions and delete keys when employees leave the organization.

questions.sourceExplanation: Option D is correct because AEAD (Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data) functions in BigQuery allow for cell-level encryption tied to specific keys. When an employee leaves, deleting their associated key renders the encrypted data permanently unreadable, as decryption becomes mathematically impossible without the key. This differs from access controls or masking, which only hide data rather than making it cryptographically unrecoverable.
questions.explanation: Removing an employee’s read permissions and cryptographically deleting that employee’s data are different requirements. AEAD key deletion only makes the intended values unreadable when key granularity, copies and key lifecycle are designed accordingly. The prompt does not specify that key ownership model, so D is conditional rather than a general offboarding rule.
